decision.detail: I walk to the payphone on the terminal wall. The receiver is cold. I dial. She picks up on the second ring, which means she was already holding the receiver against her ear, waiting. I say: "It's me. I'm at the terminal. Van's still eight?" A pause. "Yeah." Another pause. "Okay. I'm gonna be at your door at seven-fifteen. Gloves are in the bag. Blankets I'll roll when I get there. Don't let the driver sit in the driveway. He does it. He parks in the driveway and I'm standing out there in the cold saying move, move, move." She says something. I don't really hear it. "I'm gonna sit in the ballroom. Lights are on. I'll be here. Goodnight." I hang up. I walk into the ballroom. I sit in the chair by the cable. I don't turn off the lights. I close my eyes. I wake at five. I'm at her door at seven-fifteen. The couch is a couch. It is in Pittsburgh. I am in Pittsburgh. That is the whole arithmetic. Nothing else is happening tonight. The ballroom is a ballroom. The chair is a chair. I am in the chair. That is enough. That is the whole forecast.
decision.intention: Be in the chair. Be at her door at 7:15. The couch is a couch. She is counting on me. I go.
decision.words: "It's me. I'm at the terminal. Van's still eight?" ... "Okay. I'm gonna be at your door at seven-fifteen. Gloves are in the bag. Don't let the driver sit in the driveway." ... "Goodnight."

decision.detail: I am already in the booth. The chair is still warm where I sat beside her. The tape is on the patch, spool half-turned, the head still ticking its tiny click. I don't reach for the label maker. I don't reach for the slug card. I take the regional line handset, press it to my ear, and dial the number I wrote on the back of my hand in Alma's handwriting—she gave it to me, her daughter's number, in the second minute of the interview, quiet, like she was handing over a key. I wait for the ring. I wait for the ring. It picks up. I say: "Pittsburgh. This is the Rialto. There's a recording for you." I press the send key. I watch the level meter climb, hold, fall. I do not cut the line. I sit with the hiss and the room tone and the sound of a projector changing reels in the background, and I let it play all the way through, end to end, before I set the handset down. I leave the booth the way it is. Chair pushed in. Tape on the patch. No title. No slug. No package. Just the file, moving.
decision.intention: Get Alma's voice to her daughter tonight. Not tomorrow. Not after the broadcast board decides what's usable. Tonight, before the reel is rewound and the booth is locked and the machine loses another year. One voice. One daughter. No edit. No frame. Just the sound of her, in the room, saying what she says, and the hiss of the tape underneath it. That's the whole thing. That's the piece.
decision.words: Pittsburgh. This is the Rialto. There's a recording for you.

decision.detail: I'm at the Rialto door, bag over my shoulder, the reel still warm from the housing. I don't go back inside the booth. I cross the lobby to the station patch where Rita's cable runs are coiled on the desk. I set the reel down beside her mic cable, label-side up, so whoever pulls it in the morning can read the date without guessing. I don't wind it. I don't play it. I don't say *this is the one where she says Pittsburgh*. I step back, let the bag slide off my shoulder, and walk for the bus line. One hand in my coat. The station light's still on behind me. I don't look back at it.
decision.intention: The reel needs to be where the daughter can reach it before this week's end. Rita's audio is already on the patch. My picture is the other half. Both halves in one place means it's a thing that exists, not a thing in a camera bag in a coat in a man's apartment where it will sit until it doesn't. I don't need to watch it. I don't need to be in the room. I shot it. That's the job. The job is done.
decision.words: *(none; I set the reel down and walk out)*
